caption:
🏙️ Lyon, Villeurbanne and Caluire, every building standing today by year of construction — 1860 → 2025.

The Presqu'île and the old town between the rivers fill in first, then the 19th-century quarters east of the Rhône and the factories and workers' housing of Villeurbanne. The 1930s bring the Gratte-Ciel towers, the 1970s the Part-Dieu business district, and the 2000s rebuild the old docks of Confluence at the tip of the peninsula.

📊 Data: French national building database BDNB (CSTB, Licence Ouverte), which groups adjoining buildings; heights from BD TOPO (IGN). Only 48% of the buildings have an exact recorded year: 30% were recorded as a round decade and are spread over the nearby years, 22% have no year and take the year of neighbouring buildings. Buildings older than 1860 appear from the first frame. Heights exaggerated.
🌍 Map: OpenStreetMap contributors.
